So: no animal ingredient, no 五葷 (garlic, spring onion, onion, nira, rakkyo — the Buddhist 精進 exclusion, which goes beyond veganism), and no wheat, across cakes, pizza and drinks alike. It adds 「ビーガンの方や卵、乳製品、小麦アレルギーの方も安心してお召し上がり頂けます」, naming egg, dairy and WHEAT ALLERGY explicitly. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE PIZZA IS THE HEADLINE: 「米粉の生地のカリッともっちりした美味しさ」 — a RICE FLOUR base, made in-house, with a 五葷-free tomato sauce. A gluten-free pizza is close to unobtainable in Tokyo and this one is also vegan, including a plant ベーコン. Sold by the slice at ¥350–380 and as whole pies at ¥2,800–3,040. ⚠ AND THE CAKES USE A GF SPONGE: the tiramisu is described as 手作りの豆乳チーズ over a コーヒーベースのGFスポンジ — soy-milk cheese on a gluten-free sponge. The rainbow cake, the shop’s 看板メニュー, is coloured 1枚1枚お野菜の色味をつけて — with vegetables rather than dye. ⚠ WHAT IS STILL WORTH ASKING, and this record does not claim otherwise: the shop states its recipes, not its supply chain. It publishes no statement about factory cross-contamination in bought-in ingredients the way まるごとVeganダイニング浅草 does, and it does not describe a separated kitchen. The flags below are set to the shop’s own declaration because it is explicit, first-party and repeated — but a coeliac should still ask about shared equipment, which is the one question the page does not answer. ⚠ AND THE DRINKS CARRY SOMETHING RARE: plant milks are an explicit paid option — 無調整豆乳, アーモンドミルク and オーツミルク at +¥100 each. Almost no other café in this dataset lists one at all.

tokyo_soul_food_india_suido_ba.price_note: The shop publishes a full priced card across four pages and states 「※ここで掲載するメニューの価格はすべて税込表記になります」 — all prices tax-included. ⚠ ONE DISCREPANCY ON THE SHOP'S OWN PAGE, RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER: the dinner page renders its おつまみ block twice (desktop and mobile layouts) and three items carry different prices in the two blocks — ほかほか焼き枝豆 appears at both ￥490 and ￥390, きのこのバター醤油風味 at both ￥490 and ￥390, and インドの焼きそば チョーミン at both ￥920 and ￥900. The higher figure of each pair is recorded below with the alternative noted; check in the shop. ⚠ WHY AN INDIAN KITCHEN IS THE BEST NEWS IN THIS WHOLE SHARD FOR A COELIAC, AND EXACTLY WHERE IT STOPS. Indian curry is thickened with onion, tomato, nuts and cream rather than a wheat roux, which makes it structurally unlike Japanese curry — and this shop lets you take every single curry with RICE instead of naan, including at lunch where it prints ライス大盛無料. That one substitution converts most of the card. The wheat is concentrated almost entirely in the bread: プレーンナン, ごまナン, ガーリックナン, チーズナン and ガーリックチーズナン are all wheat, and ロティ is explicitly 全粒粉, wholemeal — wholemeal is still wheat, and the word 全粒粉 on a menu misleads people constantly. ⚠ THE TWO GENUINELY PROMISING SIDES, AND THE FRYER PROBLEM THAT SITS UNDER BOTH. パパド at ￥390 is a lentil-flour chip and パコラ at ￥690 is a chickpea-batter fritter — both are naturally wheat-free forms, and they are the sort of thing a coeliac almost never gets offered in Japan. They are recorded ask, not gf, for two reasons: commercial papad is sometimes cut with wheat flour or asafoetida compounded with wheat, and both are deep-fried in oil this kitchen also uses for サモサ, whose pastry is wheat. Ask about the fryer. ⚠ THE VEGAN PICTURE IS BETTER THAN USUAL AND STILL NEEDS ONE QUESTION. ベジタブルカリー at ￥1200 is a permanent plant curry, and パコラ, ポテトのホットスパイシー炒め, スパイシーインディアントマトサラダ and 緑トマトのさっぱり漬け are all plant dishes. The question to ask is ghee and cream: North Indian kitchens routinely finish vegetable curries with butter or dairy cream, and バターチキン and チキン コルマ on the same card show this kitchen works in that idiom. ライタ is explicitly yoghurt and サグ is usually creamed. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM THAT LOOKS INDIAN AND IS NOT: インドの焼きそば チョーミン is chow mein — wheat noodles, plus a soy-based stir-fry seasoning. きのこのバター醤油風味 names 醤油 outright.

tokyo_kisetsu_kappo_katsumi.price_note: The shop publishes its whole à la carte with prices by section, plus three courses. 季節割烹 勝味 is a Shibuya kappo; the shop says it goes to market daily (毎日市場へ足を運び) and notes that the お造り盛合せ contents vary 季節や仕入れ状況で. ⚠ A KAPPO COUNTER IS THE BEST-SHAPED JAPANESE ROOM FOR A COELIAC AND THIS CARD SHOWS EXACTLY WHY, AND EXACTLY WHERE IT BREAKS. Half the menu is raw fish or salt-grilled fish — 塩焼 items are fish, salt and fire, with no sauce at all — and that is a category almost nothing else in this dataset offers. 本ししゃも塩焼 800円, 銀だら塩焼 1,300円 and きんき塩焼 (price varies seasonally, the shop states 3,800円〜4,800円) are the cleanest hot dishes here; ぎんなん at 600円 is just grilled ginkgo nuts. The お造り section is raw fish throughout. ⚠ WHERE IT BREAKS IS THE SOY, AND ON A JAPANESE CARD THE SOY IS EVERYWHERE ONCE YOU READ THE VERB. 照焼 means a soy-mirin glaze, so ぶり照焼 at 900円 is out. 煮付け means simmered in soy, so both きんき煮付け at 4,600円 and 銀だら煮付け at 1,300円 are out. 西京焼 is a miso marinade and 若狭焼 is a soy-and-sake baste. ポン酢 on the 白子ポン酢 at 1,000円 is soy plus citrus. ぬた is a vinegar-miso dressing and 胡麻和え is a sesame-and-soy one. And the sashimi itself arrives with a soy dish, so even the clean items need 塩 requested instead. ⚠ THE 揚物 AND お食事 SECTIONS ARE A CLEAN SWEEP OF WHEAT AND WORTH NAMING because several look innocent. 天ぷら盛合せ 1,200円 and 穴子一本揚 900円 are batter; とり唐揚げ 700円 and かれい唐揚げ 1,000円 are flour-dredged; 海老しんじょう and 蓮根しんじょう at 800円 are shinjo, a fish paste conventionally bound with egg white and 大和芋 but very often extended with flour. In お食事, 茶そば 500円 is green-tea soba which is conventionally wheat-cut, そうめん 600円 and 煮そうめん 700円 are wheat noodles by definition, and 冷稲庭うどん 600円 and 温稲庭うどん 700円 are Inaniwa udon — a famous regional noodle that is still entirely wheat. いそべ焼 400円 is grilled mochi wrapped in nori and brushed with soy. ⚠ THE THINGS THAT SURVIVE, PLAINLY LISTED: おにぎり 2個 500円 and 焼おにぎり 2個 500円 are rice (the yaki version is soy-brushed, the plain one is not), ご飯 200円, ぞうすい 600円 is a rice porridge worth asking about, and お新香 400円 is pickles. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THIS IS A HARD ROOM AND THERE IS NO POINT PRETENDING OTHERWISE: ぎんなん, お新香, ご飯 and おにぎり are the whole list, and ほうれん草胡麻和え at 500円 — the one green vegetable dish — is dressed with a sesame-soy that conventionally carries dashi. Courses are 羽衣 8品 5,000円, 椀久 10品 7,000円 (drinks package +2,500円) and 北州 10品 10,000円, the last by reservation and composed to the guest's preference.

tokyo_iroriann_kiraku_soba_sui.price_note: Prices come from いろり庵きらく's own brand menu pages (operator: JR東日本クロスステーション フーズカンパニー), all stated 税込. TWO CAVEATS THE OPERATOR ITSELF PRINTS: 「※店舗により価格が異なります」 — prices differ by branch — and 「※一部店舗では販売していない商品もございます」 — some branches do not carry every item. This record is the Suidobashi branch of a large JR-station chain, and the branch page (shop.jr-cross.co.jp code f13778) publishes no prices of its own, so treat these as the chain card rather than a Suidobashi guarantee. ⚠ THIS IS A STANDING-SOBA COUNTER AND NOTHING ON IT IS SAFE FOR A COELIAC — but this record is unusually well evidenced, because the operator publishes a real allergen PDF (Kiraku_allergen_20260801.pdf, dated 2026-08-01, 11 pages, linked from its News post as アレルギー情報). That PDF states in its own words: "Our restaurant uses the same equipment and utensils for cooking raw materials that contain allergens other than marked by circle. So allergen contamination has occurred unintentionally." and, decisively, "Soba and udon are boiled in the same pot." A shared soba/udon pot means the boiling water carries dissolved wheat from the udon and from the 打ち粉 dusting on the soba, so even a nominally high-buckwheat noodle is contaminated in the pot. The PDF also disclaims: "We do not offer allergy-related services, such as changing or removing ingredients" and "Allergic reactions differ to each individuals, so this list does not guarantee that allergic reactions will not occur." HONEST LIMIT OF THIS RECORD: the PDF's per-item circle matrix did NOT extract — the item names are in Adobe-Japan1 CID fonts and the circle marks are glyphs this toolchain cannot read, so only the calorie column and the prose came through. NO per-item allergen mark below is taken from that table; every gf flag here is reasoned from the dish form plus the shared-pot statement, not read off the matrix. Someone who can open the PDF visually should re-verify. Separately, kake-tsuyu at a station soba counter is めんつゆ — soy sauce, hence wheat — and it is poured over every hot bowl.

tokyo_chiisana_kankoku_apuro_t.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own site (渋谷区道玄坂1-15-8 WAVE道玄坂 1F2F — the record's Dogenzaka/Shinsen placement). ⚠ THE MOST USEFUL STRUCTURAL FACT ON THIS CARD IS THAT THE SHOP PRINTS ITS OWN INGREDIENT LISTS, and they are doing real work. Every チヂミ carries its filling in brackets — あぷろチヂミ is (ニラ/エビ/イカ/アサリ/チーズ/肉ミンチ), 海鮮 is (ニラ/エビ/イカ/アサリ), ジャガイモチーズ is (ニラ/チーズ/ジャガイモ), キムチ is (ニラ/キムチ), 激辛 is (ニラ/唐辛子/激辛ソース). That last one is the only chijimi with no animal ingredient listed — and chijimi batter is WHEAT flour regardless, so it is a vegan lead and never a gluten one. Likewise the shop states every キンパ contains (ほうれん草/ニンジン/ごぼう/カニカマ/たくらん/卵) as its base, which means every kimbap on the card carries CRAB STICK and EGG — カニカマ is a wheat-starch-bound surimi, so even ナムルキンパ, which reads vegetable, is neither vegan nor wheat-free. That single line disqualifies a whole section and you would not guess it. ⚠ THE NOODLES ARE THE OTHER TRAP AND THEY GO BOTH WAYS. サリ麺 is a wheat ramen noodle and it appears in スンドゥブラーメン, in プデチゲ (with a ¥660 麺追加) and as the 〆 of チーズタッカルビ; 辛ラーメン is Shin Ramyun, wheat. But 冷麺 Korean cold noodles are buckwheat-and-starch, and チャプチェ and its 春雨 are sweet-potato starch — genuinely not wheat, though the chapchae seasoning is soy. ⚠ Korean cooking's default seasonings are 醤油 and 味噌 and コチュジャン, and Korean gochujang and doenjang are conventionally made with wheat flour, so チゲ, ヤンニョム, カンジャン, ソース-marinated and 甘辛 dishes are all wheat by default. ⚠ VEGAN: the ナムル盛合せ at ¥968 (もやし/ほうれん草/人参/ゼンマイ, ¥418 each) is the strongest plant option, though Korean namul is dressed with sesame oil, garlic and often a fish-based seasoning. Kimchi here is unlikely to be vegan.

tokyo_asakusa_gyuuna_yadoki.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own site (台東区浅草1-23-9 — the record's Asakusa/Shin-Nakamise placement). ⚠ THE RECORD FILES THIS AS UNAGI AND THAT IS ONLY HALF RIGHT. The shop's own framing is 「やどき自慢の和牛肉と厳選した鰻」 — wagyu AND eel given equal billing, and the card is built as a grid of the two: 鰻蒲焼飯, 和牛飯, 鰻和牛飯, 牛タン飯, 鰻牛タン飯, 和牛牛タン飯, all at the same ¥3,190. Somebody arriving for a straight unagi meal has more choice than the record implies, and somebody avoiding eel still has a full card. ⚠ FOR A COELIAC THIS IS ONE OF THE HARDEST JAPANESE CATEGORIES AND THE REASON IS 蒲焼: the eel is repeatedly dipped and grilled in a soy-sugar-mirin tare, which is the technique that defines kabayaki. There is no wheat-free version. The 白焼 (plain-grilled, unglazed) eel is the exception worth knowing about — it is grilled without the tare, though it is conventionally eaten with wasabi and SOY. That distinction is the single most useful thing on this card. ⚠ Every 飯 set includes 吸い物 or 味噌汁 and pickles; both soups are dashi-based, so both are gluten and vegan questions. ⚠ VEGAN: nothing. すくいおぼろ豆腐 and ゆで落花生 are the only plant items and the tofu is normally served with soy. The 8:00–10:30 breakfast service is a genuinely useful listing — an early Asakusa breakfast is hard to find — but ととのうお茶漬け is built on やどきの出汁 and the onigiri set includes 牛汁, a beef soup.

items.en: Glazed grilled eel over rice, with clear or miso soup and pickles — half size ¥1,500
items.note: 蒲焼 means the eel is repeatedly dipped in a soy-sugar tare between grillings. Soy sauce is wheat by default and there is no unglazed version of this dish.

tokyo_kakigoya_suidobashi_sanc.price_note: ⚠ THE URL ON THE RECORD IS DEAD, BUT THE SHOP IS VERY MUCH OPEN. The record cites https://kakigoyasuidobashi.owst.jp/ , which returns HTTP 404 with an empty body — the Ebica/owst page is gone. The shop's live official page is https://ghjr400.gorp.jp/ , which was showing bookable availability every day from 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-13 when checked, and it also runs a shop-run HotPepper card (last updated 2024-03-28). Both were cross-checked to the same address, 東京都千代田区神田三崎町1-4-8 愛光舎ビルB1, so they are the same shop and not a near-name collision; the record's website field should be repointed at the gorp address. ⚠ SHOP FACTS: two minutes from JR Suidobashi; open 17:00–24:00 (L.O. 23:30) with a LUNCH SERVICE 11:00–14:30 as well; 年中無休, no closing day at all; 90 seats with four private rooms (up to 48 at a table, up to 30 on tatami) and whole-venue hire from 30 to 90; all major cards and J-Debit; children welcome; heated-tobacco smoking allowed at the table but paper cigarettes only in the smoking room; Chinese-speaking staff. ⚠ THE OYSTERS ARE THE POINT AND THE SOURCING IS UNUSUALLY WELL DOCUMENTED. The shop states its oysters come direct from producers in Miyagi, Hokkaido and Iwate, and that it serves only 生食用 (raw-grade) stock that has cleared Miyagi's stricter standards. There is a running all-you-can-eat 缶焼き (can-steamed) oyster course. ⚠ THE DIET SHAPE HERE IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH READING CAREFULLY. Oysters are shellfish, so nothing in the headline section is vegan — but a plain raw or steamed oyster is one of the very few izakaya foods that is genuinely wheat-free, since it is cooked in its own shell with nothing added. THE WHEAT ARRIVES WITH THE ACCOMPANIMENT, NOT THE OYSTER: raw oysters are served with ponzu (soy-based) and the cooked ones are frequently finished with soy or cheese, and the shop's own カキフライ sits in a shared fryer with the karaage and the tempura. Order 生カキ or 蒸しカキ and ask for lemon and salt rather than ponzu, and this becomes one of the more workable shops in the dataset for a coeliac visitor who eats seafood. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN the pickings are thin but real and all sit in the 即肴 cold-plate section: 枝豆 ¥429, きゅうり一本漬 ¥462, 塩昆布ピリ辛きゅうり ¥495 and 冷やしトマト ¥418, each with the caveat noted on the item. 冷奴 ¥429 is tofu and would be the substantial one, but chilled tofu is conventionally topped with bonito flakes and soy — ask for it plain. ⚠ PRICES: the HotPepper card is dated 2024-03-28, so treat these as roughly two years old. The gorp page currently advertises banquet courses with two hours of drinks from ¥2,980 and the HotPepper card from ¥4,500 — a wide gap, so confirm which is current when booking. A separate two-hour drinks-only option is advertised at ¥1,980.

items.note: The shop's core product, stated to be raw-grade stock from Miyagi producers meeting that prefecture's stricter standards. ⚠ The oyster itself contains no wheat — the question is entirely what comes with it. Raw oysters are served with ponzu as standard, and ponzu is soy-based, so ask for LEMON AND SALT instead and this is clean. Shellfish, so never vegan.
Same caveat as the Miyagi: clean in itself, the ponzu is the wheat. Ask for lemon.

items.ja: ソーセージ盛り合わせ
items.note: Pork. Sausage fillers commonly include wheat rusk, and they are usually served with mustard and ketchup.

Garlic cloves fried whole — plant-based in its ingredients, which makes it a near-miss. It goes into the same oil as the oyster fry, the karaage and the prawn, so a coeliac cannot have it, and the coating is usually a dusted flour or starch.
Same story as the garlic: potatoes are plant-based, but the fryer is shared with breadcrumbed oysters and karaage, and frozen chips frequently carry a flour coating. Not usable for coeliac disease.

⚠ On paper the best vegan main in the shop — fried tofu, no meat, no dairy. Two real catches: it is normally served topped with BONITO FLAKES and soy sauce, and it is reheated in the shared fryer. Ask for it plain with ginger and spring onion, and ask whether it is grilled rather than refried.
Chicken, floured and fried, marinated in soy.
Soy-marinated and coated in wheat flour or a wheat-containing starch blend.
Squid, floured and fried.
Whole small prawns, floured and fried.
Surimi — fish paste bound with wheat starch or flour, then fried.
Pork; kimchi commonly contains salted shrimp and the seasoning may carry wheat.

⚠ A whole salted fish, grilled, served with grated daikon and a wedge of lemon — one of the cleanest cooked dishes in any Japanese izakaya for a coeliac who eats fish, because the seasoning is salt. Confirm nothing is brushed on and skip the soy sauce.
Salt-grilled, so the same reasoning as the hokke — clean unless a sauce is added. Autumn fish.
Grilled whole with the roe. Salt-seasoned as a rule; confirm.
Grilled whole squid is basted with soy sauce as standard — wheat.
Cured then flame-seared. The cure is the wheat question — see the sashimi version.

items.ja: 当店自慢ソース焼きそば
items.note: Wheat noodles in a wheat-containing Worcestershire-style sauce, normally finished with bonito flakes.
Rice, but fried rice is seasoned with soy sauce and the tendon is pre-braised in it. Beef.

items.ja: おにぎり（梅・鮭・明太）
items.en: Rice ball — plum, salmon or cod roe
items.note: ⚠ The 梅 (umeboshi) one is the only genuinely plant-based filling of the three — salmon and mentaiko are both fish. Plain salted rice with a pickled plum has no wheat and no animal ingredient; the caveats are that the nori wrapper is sometimes a seasoned type carrying soy sauce, and that bought-in ume paste is occasionally cut with dashi. Ask for 梅 and check the nori.

items.ja: お茶漬け（梅・鮭・明太）
items.en: Rice in tea broth — plum, salmon or cod roe
items.note: Unlike the onigiri, this one is not rescuable by choosing the plum: ochazuke broth is a dashi-and-soy stock, or a commercial sachet containing both. Fish and wheat regardless of topping.

items.ja: ハチミツバニラアイス
items.note: The only dessert on the card. Dairy and honey — animal on both counts.
